newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Competition proposed in S.Korea electricity sector.
newsitem.headline: Competition proposed in S.Korea electricity sector.

text.p: South Korea's Fair Trade Commission on Thursday proposed the introduction of partial competition into the country's electricity production and sales sectors.
A report from the commission said entry barriers should be lifted on electricity generation and retail sales in certain areas. Further details were not given.
Currently state-run Korea Electric Power Corp monopolises electricity production and distribution.
The report said the introduction of such competition would help reduce electricity fares and improve management efficiency at Korea Electric.
It also proposed that large consumers of liquefied natural gas (LNG) should be allowed to import directly, instead of purchasing from the state Korea Gas Corp which currently monopolises LNG imports.
A heavy consumer like Pohang Iron and Steel Co would benefit from direct LNG imports by saving purchase expenses, the report said.
South Korea, which relies on imports for all of its LNG demand, is expected to see its annual demand rising to 20.21 million tonnes in the year 2000 from 9.18 million tonnes in 1996.
The demand is estimated to rise further to 28.55 million tonnes in the year 2010, the report said, quoting data compiled by the trade ministry.
It said these proposals were subject to discussions with the trade ministry.
